ShortDescription.Value: Wider pedestrian crossings, shaped one junction at a time, plus diagonal crossings through the middle of a junction. Room for people to cross side by side.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Better Crosswalks
A crossing in Cities: Skylines II is a thin painted band that a queue of citizens shuffles across in single file. This mod widens the band and the strip people walk on together, so a crowd spreads out across it instead of filing over — and it lets you shape crossings one at a time, or run them corner to corner through the middle of a junction.
## Width
One slider, as a percentage of whatever the crossing was drawn with rather than an absolute figure. Crossings are not uniform to begin with — a side street's is narrow, a boulevard's is not — and one absolute value would flatten that, so everything scales together and keeps its proportions. It starts at 150%, and goes from 25% to 400%.
A floor and a ceiling in metres are there for the cases where a proportion is not what you want: "no crossing narrower than 4m" is a sensible rule, "every crossing exactly 4m" usually is not.
## One junction at a time
The toolbar button opens a tool. Click a junction, then a crossing on it, and five rings appear on that crossing:
- either end — drag to swing that end up or down the road, for a crossing set at an angle rather than square across - the middle — drag to slide the whole crossing towards or away from the junction - either side — drag to pull it wider or narrower
Nothing you do to one crossing touches its neighbours. There are buttons too, if you would rather not drag: narrower and wider, "same for all the crossings here", and a reset for the crossing or for the whole junction. Everything set with the tool is saved with the city.
## Crossings through the middle
Junctions where four or more roads meet can take crossings corner to corner through the middle — a scramble crossing, the kind Shibuya is known for. They are on by default, and the tool edits and removes them like any other crossing. Turn them off in settings and any already in the city are cleared out.
## How it works
A crossing is not part of the road's cross-section. It is a pedestrian lane laid across the carriageway, and the painted zebra is that lane's mesh. This mod writes the width of that lane on the lanes the game lays, and lets the game's own lane pipeline do everything else. No geometry of its own, no Harmony patches, and the road itself never gets wider.
Everything was worked out by decompiling and tracing the game's own assemblies. The full record — including the defects found in them, and the approaches that were tried and abandoned — is on the GitHub page.
## Applying it to a city you already have
Nothing to do. Change the setting and every crossing in the city follows immediately, including the ones already standing. "Apply to existing crossings" is there for the rare case where one gets missed.
## Removing it
Settings → Maintenance → "Remove this mod's data from the city", then save. Every crossing goes back to the width its asset author chose, every crossing this mod added is taken out, and the mod switches itself off so nothing puts them back before you save. The save is then exactly as it would have been if the mod had never run.
Publish.ChangeLog:
The crossing tool is reachable again.
1.0.0 shipped without its toolbar button. The button is the only way to open the crossing tool, so none of the per-junction editing could be used at all — clicking a junction, resizing one crossing, adding or removing crossings through the middle. The width settings were unaffected and worked throughout.
The cause was a check this mod made before registering the button, on an assumption about what it meant. It reported whether anything had already been added to that part of the interface, not whether that part of the interface existed, so the button was skipped depending on which other mods happened to load first.
Nothing else changed. If 1.0.0 was doing what you wanted, this only adds the button back.
